newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral speaks to Pakistan's Sharif on phone.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral speaks to Pakistan's Sharif on phone.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral telephoned his Pakistani counterpart Nawaz Sharif on Friday and the leaders agreed to maintain direct contacts, the United News of India (UNI) said.
The main purpose of Gujral's initiative was to set up a direct line of communication with Sharif, UNI said, quoting a Indian Foreign Ministry statement.
The conversation, which lasted for about ten minutes, was "very warm and cordial", it said.
Gujral and Sharif are scheduled to hold bilateral talks on May 12 ahead of a three-day summit of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) in the capital of the Maldives, Male.
The statement said both the leaders looked forward to their forthcoming meeting in Male.
The meeting would follow two rounds of high-level talks which resumed in March after three years of bitter recriminations between the longstanding foes.

It would be the first meeting between the prime ministers of the two countries since April 1993, when Nawaz Sharif and then Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao met on the sidelines of a SAARC conference, Indian officials said on Thursday.

Pakistani President Farooq Khan Leghari met Rao in May 1995, also on the sidelines of a SAARC meeting, and talked at length about Kashmir, which has been divided between the two nations since shortly after they won independence in 1947.
Bilateral peace talks had broken down in January 1994 over Kashmir, the source of two of the three wars which the neighbouring countries have fought since independence.
Negotiations resumed in March between the foreign secretaries -- the highest ranking civil servants in the foreign ministries.
Gujral, who was foreign minister under his predecessor, ousted prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda, met Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan on April 9.

Gujral was sworn in as prime minister 12 days later and has kept the foreign ministry portfolio for himself in his centre-left government, vowing to pursue his efforts to improve relations with Pakistan.
